\section[justificar]{justificar — to justify}

\label{lesson:ES-C586-justificar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to warn, then the Spanish for the warning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: justificar}
\textbf{justificar} — \textquotedblleft{}to justify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tienes que justificar los gastos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You have to justify the expenses.}
\end{quote}

Spelling: \emph{justifiqué}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{justificar} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{iustificare} 'to make right', built on \emph{iustus} 'right, lawful' and \emph{facere} 'to make' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{justificar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{justificar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{justificar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to warn, then the Spanish for the warning, then say \emph{justificar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does justificar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To justify\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la justificación]{la justificación — the justification}

\label{lesson:ES-C586-justificacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the warning, then the Spanish for to justify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la justificación}
\textbf{la justificación} — \textquotedblleft{}the justification\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No hay justificación para eso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There is no justification for that.}
\end{quote}

Often after \emph{no hay}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{justificación} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{iustificatio}, built on \emph{iustificare} 'to make right', from \emph{iustus} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la justificación}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la justificación}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la justificación}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the warning, then the Spanish for to justify, then say \emph{la justificación} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la justificación mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The justification\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la excusa]{la excusa — the excuse}

\label{lesson:ES-C586-excusa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to justify, then the Spanish for the justification.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la excusa}
\textbf{la excusa} — \textquotedblleft{}the excuse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tiene una excusa para todo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He has an excuse for everything.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Poner excusas} — to make excuses.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{excusa} is built on \emph{excusar}, inherited from Latin \emph{excusare} 'to free from blame', \emph{ex} + \emph{causa} 'case, charge' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[el pretexto]{el pretexto — the pretext}

\label{lesson:ES-C586-pretexto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the justification, then the Spanish for the excuse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el pretexto}
\textbf{el pretexto} — \textquotedblleft{}the pretext\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Usó la lluvia como pretexto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He used the rain as a pretext.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Con el pretexto de} — on the pretext of.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pretexto} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{praetextus} 'a cover, a show', built on \emph{praetexere} 'to weave in front', from \emph{texere} 'to weave' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

\section[demostrar]{demostrar — to show, to prove}

\label{lesson:ES-C586-demostrar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the excuse, then the Spanish for the pretext.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: demostrar}
\textbf{demostrar} — \textquotedblleft{}to show, to prove\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Los datos demuestran que tengo razón.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The data show that I am right.}
\end{quote}

Stem change o$\to$ue: \emph{demuestro}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{demostrar} is inherited from Latin \emph{demonstrare} 'to point out', built on \emph{monstrare} 'to show', the verb behind \emph{mostrar} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the excuse, then the Spanish for the pretext, then say \emph{demostrar} again
